evidence_items.publisher: American Journal of Roentgenology; abstract hosted by PubMed
evidence_items.explanation: The randomized study demonstrates useful assistance on chest CT examinations while humans continue interpreting them. It measures reading time, not the relative effort of developing assistance and full replacement.

evidence_items.publisher: Insights into Imaging / European Society of Radiology; abstract hosted by PubMed
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, results for users of diagnostic algorithms
evidence_items.explanation: The survey reports limited workload benefits for many users of diagnostic assistance. This qualifies an inference from tool availability to practical ease, but it does not compare development requirements with full replacement; precise survey fieldwork dates were not identified.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved study compares the development effort or capability requirements of assistance and full replacement for the same occupation.
The studies measure workload and reading time, not the claimed causal difference in difficulty.
Evidence from radiology alone cannot establish the size of the advantage across occupations.
